citation.title: Simultaneous feedback control of plasma rotation and stored energy on the DIII-D tokamak
citation.authors: J.T. Scoville, D.A. Humphreys, J.R. Ferron, P. Gohil

topic: DIII-D real-time PCS control of stored energy and impurity-ion rotation using co/counter neutral beam mix
own_question: Can a simple linear energy/momentum balance model support PID control of stored energy and rotation via co/counter beams?
actual_method_and_evidence: Second-order source-sink model with empirical loss factors fE and fm. The authors report these factors are near 1 in steady phases of one discharge (124720). The model is driven with measured beam powers and compared to measurements in text-only figures. A delayed state-space simulation with orthogonalized PID control is followed by an experimental demonstration in discharge 126056. CER impurity rotation is used, but not temperature. There is no nowcasting, no BES/ECEI, and no held-out validation.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: CER-derived impurity rotation has been used as a feedback-controlled quantity in tokamak plasma control, with computation/filter delays modeled.
claim_checks.qualification: The quantity is rotation, not Ti. The 10 ms delay is the authors' assumed simulation delay, not measured report arrival times. DIII-D, not KSTAR.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Rotation delay of about 10 ms is assumed in simulation for filter plus CER analysis. Actual CES/CER report latency is not measured.
validation_if_relevant: Single-discharge consistency check plus simulation. No train/test split.
forbidden_inferences: Do not cite as evidence of CES temperature nowcasting or Ti latency
Do not cite 10 ms as KSTAR timing
Do not claim the model was validated across campaigns
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional context showing that CER-based quantities can enter real-time control. It is off-target for estimating current impurity-temperature reports; exclude unless an applications sentence is retained.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
